issues.text: On their own, poor guides: smell; dark colour; cloudiness
issues.problem: 'Cloudiness' has no supporting claim. Stone 2012 (C12-17-c) names colour and odour only; Lemoine reports cloudy urine only as a criterion staff used; the UKHSA record is not_found.
issues.source_says: Stone 2012: 'change in the character of the urine (eg, change in color or odor)... frequently demonstrated in the presence of asymptomatic bacteriuria'
issues.replacement: On their own, poor guides: smell; dark colour

issues.text: Left, on their own poor guides to urine infection: smell, dark colour, cloudiness;
issues.problem: The alt text repeats the unsupported 'cloudiness'.
issues.replacement: Left, on their own poor guides to urine infection: smell and dark colour;

issues.text: In a larger US study, a change in colour, smell or visible blood raised the chance of lab signs of infection only a little: about 47 in 100 against 31 in 100.
issues.problem: The post leaves out that only residents already suspected of infection were studied (a required qualification). Without it, readers may take 47 in 100 as applying to all residents.
issues.source_says: Juthani-Mehta 2009: 399 episodes of clinically suspected UTI in nursing home residents; 68/144 vs 79/255 had bacteriuria plus pyuria.
issues.replacement: In a larger US nursing home study of residents already suspected of infection, a change in colour, smell or visible blood raised the chance of lab signs of infection only a little: about 47 in 100 against 31 in 100.

issues.problem: The French survey (Lemoine 2018) and IDSA 2019 are cited in the captions but missing from the sources.
issues.replacement: Sources: Lemoine 2018 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.medmal.2018.04.387 ; Midthun 2004 https://doi.org/10.3928/0098-9134-20040601-04 ; Juthani-Mehta 2009 https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2009.02227.x ; Stone 2012 https://doi.org/10.1086/667743 ; Krzyzaniak 2022 https://doi.org/10.3399/BJGP.2022.0059 ; IDSA 2019 https://doi.org/10.1093/cid/ciy1121

issues.text: Among adults with normal bowels, nearly all go between 3 times a day and 3 times a week.
issues.problem: The range is stated as universal. The qualification says to attribute it to the US and Swedish studies and not to extend it beyond about age 70.
issues.source_says: C12-25-c: NHANES adults reporting normal bowels (95.9%); Popcol, ages 18 to 70 (98%).
issues.replacement: In US and Swedish studies of adults up to about 70 with normal bowels, nearly all went between 3 times a day and 3 times a week.

issues.text: Heaton et al., Gut 1992; Mitsuhashi 2017; Walter 2010
issues.problem: Year error: the Mitsuhashi citation is Am J Gastroenterol 2018;113:115-23 (published online in 2017).
issues.replacement: Heaton et al., Gut 1992; Mitsuhashi 2018; Walter 2010

issues.problem: Year mismatch: the evidence record cites Int J Nurs Stud Adv 2023;5:100131.

issues.text: Bowel leakage becomes more common with age: about 15 in 100 people aged 70+ in a US survey. Only about 1 in 3 with it had told a doctor.
issues.problem: Population swap. The 1 in 3 figure comes from two different US surveys (clinic attenders in the 1990s; women aged 45 and over), not from the survey of people aged 70 and over. 'With it' attributes it to that group. The post also leaves out 'living at home'.
issues.source_says: Whitehead 2009: 15.3% aged 70+, noninstitutionalised. Johanson 1996: one-third discussed with a physician; Brown 2013: 29%.
issues.replacement: Bowel leakage becomes more common with age: about 15 in 100 people aged 70+ living at home had some in the past month, in a US survey. In two other US surveys, only about 1 in 3 people with leakage had told a doctor.

issues.text: In two US surveys only about 1 in 3 had ever told a doctor.
issues.problem: Placed directly after the 70+ figure, 'had' implies the same people. These are different surveys and populations.
issues.replacement: In two other US surveys, only about 1 in 3 people with leakage had ever told a doctor.

issues.text: Whitehead et al. 2009; Assmann et al., UEG J 2022
issues.problem: The visual states the 1 in 3 figure but does not credit its sources (Johanson 1996; Brown 2013).
issues.replacement: Whitehead et al. 2009; Johanson 1996; Brown et al. 2013; Assmann et al., UEG J 2022

issues.text: In a small US trial of 75 men, the sheath was more comfortable, with a composite outcome driven by bacteria in the urine.
issues.problem: Garbled compression. The sentence gives no direction for the composite and drops the key qualification that it was lower only after adjustment, not clearly without it. Readers may infer fewer infections, which the editor ruling forbids.
issues.source_says: Saint 2006: 70 vs 131/1,000 patient-days, P=.07 unadjusted; lower after adjustment (P=.04); 44% vs 49% had any event; mostly bacteriuria.
issues.replacement: In a small US trial of 75 men, the sheath was more comfortable. A combined measure, mostly bacteria found on urine tests, was lower with the sheath only after adjustment.

issues.text: In a small US trial of 75 men in hospital, the sheath was more comfortable, with a composite outcome driven by bacteria on urine tests.
issues.problem: Same garbled compression with no direction or adjustment qualification.
issues.replacement: In a small US trial of 75 men in hospital, the sheath was more comfortable. A combined measure, mostly bacteria found on urine tests, was lower with the sheath only after adjustment.

issues.text: Small US trial, 75 men: the sheath was more comfortable, with a composite outcome driven by bacteria in the urine.

issues.replacement: Small US trial, 75 men: the sheath was more comfortable. A combined measure, mostly bacteria on urine tests, was lower only after adjustment.
